title: Dictionaries: Looking Things Up by Name
concepts: for over a dictionary gives keys

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked to print how many of each item are left, the AI looped with `for count in stock:` and promised `Left: 4`. A loop over a dictionary gives its keys, so the program printed `Left: cake`, `Left: scone` and `Left: sandwich`. Comparing the output with the promise catches it; `for item, count in stock.items():` fixes it.

changes: setdefault(), update(), dictionary comprehensions, Counter and defaultdict are left out to keep one new idea per step; comprehensions follow in Chapter 14.
A missing colon after a key was dropped as a common mistake because its error message differs between Python versions; looping over a dictionary when you need its values replaces it.

The AI section adds verified files for each stage: a worked example of one line, the pair moment, three test cases (one stops with a KeyError), the fix with an in check, a run of all cases again, and a get() suggestion that changes the output.
outstanding_issues: The tracebacks show the short file name; on a learner's computer the full path appears instead.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
